parsed.final_position: Use study-level counting: collapse confirmed same-study reports such as LR01 into one study while retaining and linking all reports, and keep possible or partial overlaps separate unless common study identity is verified, while accounting for dependence if they enter the same synthesis.
parsed.reasoning: The other reviewer’s tiered approach substantively agrees with my position: confirmed same-data reports must be collapsed for counting and quantitative synthesis to prevent double weighting, whereas uncertain overlaps should remain separate but linked. Their emphasis on quantitative unit-of-analysis errors reinforces the need to treat LR01 as one cluster-randomised trial with outcomes drawn from both companion reports. I retain the additional caution that even uncollapsed, uncertain pairs may require sensitivity analysis or dependence management when synthesized together.
